cef2463b118e51521250c6c758f83065cbfc8c70: Campitello Matese is a modestly sized, little-known resort: 19 km of runs for an intimate skiing experience, far from the bustle of the big resorts. This is where people come for calm, authenticity and no queues at the lifts. Campitello Matese's family reputation is well deserved: dedicated beginner areas, well-groomed green runs and a friendly atmosphere at the foot of the lifts. It is one of the most reassuring resorts in the Apennines for getting children started on skiing. Campitello Matese's modest altitude, with the base at 1417 m and the summit at 1827 m, makes it sensitive to climate variations. January and February remain the safest months for optimal snow cover. Outside this window, checking the snow reports before setting off is strongly advised. The day pass at 48€ places Campitello Matese among the intermediate resorts on budget: neither cheap nor exorbitant. The quality of the ski area and facilities justifies this price for most skiers. In short, Campitello Matese does not rival the giants of skiing, and does not claim to. It is an honest destination, often underrated, that deserves to be (re)discovered.
cefdeb841a867aa34a50f877c8cf31d7815db1a6: Bad Kleinkirchheim offers 103 km of well-marked runs — a mid-sized ski area, ideal for spending 4 to 5 days without ever doing exactly the same thing twice. The 24 lifts are generally sufficient to handle the crowds in high season. Bad Kleinkirchheim has kept an authentic mountain village identity, far from the concrete resorts of the 1970s. People come here for the clean air, the unspoilt landscapes and a friendly atmosphere that stands out from the industrialisation of skiing in some large ski areas. Bad Kleinkirchheim's altitude (1087 m at the base, 2055 m at the top) helps it keep reasonable snow cover in midwinter. January and February are the most reliable; in December and March, it is worth checking conditions before finalising a booking. A stay in Bad Kleinkirchheim is clearly on the expensive side: 70€ for a day lift pass, plus accommodation and mountain restaurants among the most expensive in the Alps. It is the price of excellence — but you should be aware of it before you go. In short: Bad Kleinkirchheim keeps its promises. A Northern Alps resort that should suit most profiles without disappointing.
